records.public_claim_text: For the purposes of this guideline, the primary stakeholders are the patient, healthcare professional, regulatory authority, and industry.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: For the purposes of this guideline, the primary stakeholders are the patient, healthcare professional, regulatory authority, and industry.

records.public_claim_text: Failure Mode Effects Analysis (FMEA) (I.2) FMEA (see IEC 60812) provides for an evaluation of potential failure modes for processes and their likely effect on outcomes and/or product performance.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: Failure Mode Effects Analysis (FMEA) (I.2) FMEA (see IEC 60812) provides for an evaluation of potential failure modes for processes and their likely effect on outcomes and/or product performance.

records.public_claim_text: Failure Mode, Effects, and Criticality Analysis (FMECA) (I.3) FMEA might be extended to incorporate an investigation of the degree of severity of the consequences, their respective probabilities of occurrence, and their detectability, thereby becoming a Failure Mode Effect and Criticality Analysis (FMECA; see IEC 60812).

records.public_claim_text: Fault Tree Analysis (FTA) (I.4) The FTA tool (see IEC 61025) is an approach that assumes failure of the functionality of a product or process.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: Fault Tree Analysis (FTA) (I.4) The FTA tool (see IEC 61025) is an approach that assumes failure of the functionality of a product or process.

records.public_claim_text: Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points (HACCP) (I.5) HACCP is a systematic, proactive, and preventive tool for assuring product quality, reliability, and safety (see WHO Technical Report Series No 908, 2003 Annex 7).
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points (HACCP) (I.5) HACCP is a systematic, proactive, and preventive tool for assuring product quality, reliability, and safety (see WHO Technical Report Series No 908, 2003 Annex 7).

records.public_claim_text: Hazard Operability Analysis (HAZOP) (I.6) HAZOP (see IEC 61882) is based on a theory that assumes that risk events are caused by deviations from the design or operating intentions.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: Hazard Operability Analysis (HAZOP) (I.6) HAZOP (see IEC 61882) is based on a theory that assumes that risk events are caused by deviations from the design or operating intentions.

records.public_claim_text: Preliminary Hazard Analysis (PHA) (I.7) PHA is a tool of analysis based on applying prior experience or knowledge of a hazard or failure to identify future hazards, hazardous situations and events that might cause harm, as well as to estimate their probability of occurrence for a given activity, facility, product, or system.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: Preliminary Hazard Analysis (PHA) (I.7) PHA is a tool of analysis based on applying prior experience or knowledge of a hazard or failure to identify future hazards, hazardous situations and events that might cause harm, as well as to estimate their probability of occurrence for a given activity, facility, product, or system.

records.public_claim_text: The tool consists of: (1) the identification of the possibilities that the risk event happens; (2) the qualitative evaluation of the extent of possible injury or damage to health that could result; (3) a relative ranking of the hazard using a combination of severity and likelihood of occurrence; and (4) the identification of possible remedial measures.

records.public_claim_text: It can be used for product, process, and facility design as well as to evaluate the types of hazards for the general product type, then the product class, and finally the specific product.

records.public_claim_text: Typically, hazards identified in the PHA are further assessed with other risk management tools such as those in this section.
